problem: LLM-based navigation is rarely applied to time-sensitive, safety-critical socially-aware robot navigation in human-robot interaction, and traditional RL methods lack strong spatial and semantic reasoning. LLM inference latency also limits real-time use.
motivation: Socially-aware navigation needs predictable, trustworthy robots that reason about humans and context. LLMs offer cognitive and semantic reasoning, but grounding them in real sensor data and making them fast enough for real-time control is unresolved.
key_idea: Fuse LiDAR and camera data into semantically associated contextual input for a distilled and fine-tuned LLM navigation policy, and later add a brain-cerebellum hybrid architecture for real-time performance.
insight: The abstract reports that the fine-tuned LLM does better than RL baselines in low-frequency decision-making scenarios, but inference latency is the main bottleneck. This motivates a hybrid brain-cerebellum design. No ablations are available from the abstract.
method: Multimodal fusion pipeline: integrates LiDAR and camera data, using a YOLO detector and Hungarian-algorithm association to produce semantic context for the LLM.
Knowledge distillation and fine-tuning: trains the LLM navigation model on data from a custom simulator.
Four-stage research plan: the first two stages, foundational model development and evaluation, are complete.
Planned brain-cerebellum hybrid architecture: pairs slow LLM reasoning with a fast controller for real-time performance.
Planned multi-robot social compliance: extends the framework to multiple robots.

setting.backbone: LLM (unspecified), distilled and fine-tuned; YOLO detector for perception
setting.training_data: Data from a custom simulator, used for knowledge distillation and fine-tuning (scale not given in the abstract)
setting.observation: LiDAR + camera (YOLO detections associated by the Hungarian algorithm)

results: The abstract states the fine-tuned LLM model shows robust spatial reasoning and outperforms traditional RL methods in low-frequency decision-making scenarios. It reports no numbers. Inference latency was identified as the key challenge.
limitations: High LLM inference latency prevents real-time use
Only the first two of four stages are done; there is no multi-robot or real-robot validation yet
